work.text: His head and white collar emerge from solid black; his name and the date are lettered across the top, and a skeleton's forearm lies along the bottom edge, like a ledge beneath a portrait bust.

moment.text: In Berlin, Munch became involved in an international circle of writers, artists and critics, including the Swedish dramatist and leading intellectual August Strindberg, whom he painted in 1892.
Psychologic, in the true sense of that much-abused word, are his portraits … as well as the self-portraits … these and many others serve as testimony to a sympathetic divination of character.

source.author: James Huneker
source.title: “Kubin, Munch, and Gauguin: Masters of Mystery and Hallucination”, in Ivory Apes and Peacocks

matters.text: My father was temperamentally nervous and obsessively religious—to the point of psychoneurosis. From him I inherited the seeds of madness. The angels of fear, sorrow, and death stood by my side since the day I was born.

source.author: Edvard Munch
source.title: Autobiographical notes, quoted in “Edvard Munch”

matters.text: I am writing a study of the soul as I observe myself closely and use myself as an anatomical testing-ground.
